We use Zod 4 (zod ^4). The schema package uses `looseObject` for forward compatibility, and records and project.yaml are loose objects at every level [dec-094vmt9t].

The JSON Schema is produced with Zod 4's built-in `toJSONSchema`, which removed the need for a separate dependency [dec-094vmt9t]. To regenerate the published files, run `pnpm --filter @aimem/schema build`, which refreshes `dist/record.schema.json` and `project.schema.json`. Then review the snapshot diff and update the snapshot deliberately [run-17vbsk09]. A snapshot test (`json-schema.test.ts`) guards the exported JSON Schema contract and was passing on 2026-10-11 [tst-cw10hn77].

Also, the schemas never use `.default()`. Defaults are exported as constants instead [dec-4mn8zfef].

Claims use compare-and-swap on a dedicated branch. Live claims are stored as JSON on an `aimem-live` branch. To acquire a task, a clone fetches, checks the current holder, commits and pushes. If the push is rejected, it retries, so two clones cannot both win [dec-kqfc1se7].

Consequences [dec-kqfc1se7]:
- It needs network access to the remote.
- Expired claims can be stolen after the TTL.

Claims are kept out of task files on purpose. Writing them there caused merge conflicts on every heartbeat, so durable records and fast-moving live state are separate layers [dec-g17nvbca]. An agent-written memory says the same: claim holder, heartbeat and TTL live on the `aimem-live` branch or a server, not in the task file. It is not human-verified [mem-peqcrkme].

We evaluated isomorphic-git, a pure-JS git library, and rejected it because of gaps in credentials, hooks and worktrees [dec-ghsxv3vg]. The upside would have been avoiding process spawning and simpler tests [dec-ghsxv3vg].

Instead, all git work shells out to the user's installed git binary through execa, so credentials, hooks and config behave as usual. Reimplementing git would also miss LFS, worktrees and credential helpers [dec-ndgz6y7a]. The trade-off is that git must be installed, which is true for every target user [dec-ndgz6y7a]. Tests use real temporary repos instead of mocks [dec-ghsxv3vg].

Record ids are random so that parallel branches never collide. Counters collide when two branches add records at the same time [dec-j2t35mx0].

Ids are a type prefix plus 8 random Crockford base32 characters. The id in frontmatter is authoritative, and the slug may drift [dec-j2t35mx0].

The trade-offs are that ids are not sortable by time, and validation fails on duplicates [dec-j2t35mx0].

After upgrading Biome to 2.5, `biome migrate` rewrote `recommended: true` to `preset: none`, which silently disabled all lint rules [mem-rj2t0xj9][inc-242wrkm4]. Lint kept passing on everything because nothing was being checked, so any lint problem could have reached main unnoticed [inc-242wrkm4].

**Resolution:** It was noticed in the migrate output and fixed the same session (2026-10-12). The preset was set back to recommended and verified by adding an explicit `any`, which must trigger a `noExplicitAny` warning [inc-242wrkm4][mem-rj2t0xj9].

**Prevention:** Probe lint after any lint config change [inc-242wrkm4].

Schema validation can fail with V002 when an unquoted `content_sha` is made up only of digits. YAML reads an all-digit scalar as an integer, so the value is no longer a string. For example, a placeholder sha of zeros became the number 0 and failed the string check on `source.content_sha` [mem-hrm4q190].

The fix is to quote hashes and ids that could be all digits when writing frontmatter [mem-hrm4q190].

Note that this record has trust="agent", so it is not human-verified.

aimem authenticates to Google using a service account that can read one shared inbox folder, rather than per-user OAuth [mem-j4yeeebg]. The stated reasons are least privilege and no consent screens for non-developers. Per-user OAuth remains an option [mem-j4yeeebg].

This fits the broader decision to ingest from Google Docs and Sheets through connectors (upload and Google Drive in v1), which produce read-only, externally-owned records [dec-8hscg239].

The records don't describe a way to keep private, never-committed notes. They say knowledge lives as markdown records committed to git in `.aimem/` [dec-3by2wh28], and that roles only affect ranking, not access, so anyone with repo access can read everything [dec-2znaykpx]. The only things stored outside git are the rebuildable vector cache [sch-nygqk0ka] and live claims, which sit on a separate git branch [sch-3a3jkgmm]. None of those is a place for private notes.

Token counts are estimated with a chars/4 heuristic: the number of characters divided by four, with a per-model override available [dec-nppkpt6e]. The same heuristic applies to all budgets. An optional real tokenizer could be installed later [dec-nppkpt6e].

The reason is that exact tokenizers differ per model and add a heavy dependency [dec-nppkpt6e]. The estimate can be off by roughly 10–20%, so per-section limits are given some headroom [dec-nppkpt6e].

For the budget itself, the default is 4000 tokens unless project.yaml sets briefing.budget_tokens [mem-q9krtm0g].

It depends on the project mode:

- **Solo mode:** Yes. Solo mode implies `agent_commits: commit`, so agents commit their own notebook changes [dec-ek66gxgx].
- **Team mode:** No, by default. Agents only stage changes, and humans commit them along with their code [dec-ek66gxgx].
- **`pr` option:** This is also available as an alternative [dec-ek66gxgx].

A new decision with no explicit status gets **proposed**. This is set by `DEFAULT_STATUS.decision = proposed`, matching the proposed → accepted/rejected lifecycle in spec 03 [dec-9h7m0yg3]. Agents must pass `--status accepted` when a human has already agreed [dec-9h7m0yg3].

History: an earlier schema draft had `DEFAULT_STATUS.decision = accepted`, which wasn't in the spec. That was flagged in a handoff, which is agent-written and not human-verified [hnd-qp6gjbe5]. The verified decision record above supersedes it [dec-9h7m0yg3].
